summary: The candidate removes timing-dependent double charging for equal-sized ranks by synchronizing one world-group baseline and reserving later pools locally, but retains an equal per-rank cap that rejects aggregate-fitting heterogeneous pipeline-stage allocations.

tests.command: recorded-base deterministic actual host_memory_budget_bytes reproduction with 100 then 60 GiB readings, four local ranks, and a 20 GiB request
tests.what_was_measured: The actual base returned 22.5 then 12.5 GiB although four 20 GiB pools fit within 90 GiB usable initial memory.
Four real Gloo processes all received a 22.5 GiB primary budget; later sidecars received 2.5 GiB from the cached baseline without another collective.

tests.command: independent candidate boundary: 100 GiB available, 10 GiB reserve, four local ranks, heterogeneous requests 30+20+20+20 GiB
tests.what_was_measured: The 90 GiB aggregate fits the 90 GiB usable host memory, but the 30 GiB rank is rejected by the 22.5 GiB equal-share cap.

gpu_execution.evidence: Tests exercised CPU host accounting and real Gloo collectives. One AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950 GPU was visible, but no GPU computation was relevant or claimed.

remaining_counterexamples: Heterogeneous pipeline stages or other in-job groups with unequal per-rank pool sizes can fit in aggregate yet be rejected when one rank exceeds the retained equal host share; e.g. 30+20+20+20 GiB fits 90 GiB usable but 30 GiB exceeds 22.5 GiB per rank.
Separately launched jobs sharing a host are outside the candidate's world process group and cannot share its cached snapshot/accounting.
remaining_limitations: No 8xH200 GLM-5.2-W4AFP8 weights or workload were available.
Only one AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950 GPU was available; no full-model, H200, multi-node, or real heterogeneous-PP serving reproduction was performed.
No native files changed, so native rebuilding was not applicable.
